content:
I am working on formalising CM Abelian varieties (#Project intentions > #46 Formalising CM Abelian Varieties ), and was wondering what would be the right definition to use. Shimura defines the inclusion F →+* End⁰(A) over the algebraic closure of the field of definition of A, but most people would probably define this morphism over the base field (at least that is how I learnt it) - this also helps define potentially CM later on. I wanted to know what others thought.

Furthermore, I was considering defining it something like this:

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
variable (A : Over (Spec ↧K))
variable [IsProper A.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral A.hom] [AddGrpObj A]

-- this is already defined as `preCMType` in my repository
structure CMType (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] [IsCMField F] where
  partition : Set (F →+* ℂ)
  partition_condition : ∀ φ : (F →+* ℂ), φ ∈ partition ↔
    (conj : ℂ →+* ℂ).comp φ ∈ partitionᶜ

structure CMStructure (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] [IsCMField F] where
  incl : F →+* End⁰(A)
  -- [F : ℚ] = 2g

But, there are also other definitions. Oort, in his notes, just requires that F is a commutative semi-simple algebra of rank 2g , Milne, in his notes on Shimura varieties, takes care of the dimension part using homology groups (I am not sure that's a great formulation though). I have also seen definitions which say abelian varieties of type (F, Φ), where the CM Type comes into play.
I am just unsure what is the right definition to use, and wanted to know what others thought.

I think one should take algebraic closure, otherwise there are no CM elliptic curves over Q (the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve over a characteristic zero field F embeds into F via invariant differential).
But then, CM would be the same as potentially CM, right (unless I'm missing something silly)?

You're right. People actually say "let E/Q be a CM elliptic curve" and the question is whether one wants to allow this "abuse of notation" which is occurring everywhere in the literature.

If E/Q and F/Q have CM then ExF has CM in the sense of Oort but I suspect there won't in general be a degree 4 number field in End^0 if E and F aren't isogenous.

I think the way to go forwards here is to establish a definition and then document what is going on extremely well. I haven't thought about PEL Shimura varieties in this generality for a long time but it might be worth brushing up on the kinds of structures they want to consider before making any final decisions.

Getting definitions right is one of the hardest parts of formalisation.
Oh, given that Oort is a world expert in PEL Shimura varieties I realise that I know what the answer is going to be.

Kevin Buzzard said:

I think the way to go forwards here is to establish a definition and then document what is going on extremely well.

I was curious what you meant by 'document what's going on extremely well'. I'm guessing you mean having a catalogue of results, which says which ones are CM and which ones aren't, right?
I just mean "write very clear definition and module docstrings explaining which conventions we're using, what other conventions there are, and the consequences of the choices we've made".
This way, whenever someone hovers over a definition with CM in, they see an explanation of exactly what is meant.
